title: Command & Conquer: Renegade

engine.name: Westwood 3D (Renegade engine)
engine.evidence: Game.exe links 2000-06-01 and imports binkw32/mss32 plus BandTest.dll; content ships as .mix archives under Data; Scripts.dll provides the game's script library; the shipped free dedicated server (RenegadeFDS) runs the same simulation.
engine.notes: Three separate executables with three different jobs: Renegade.exe is the Steam launcher (launcher.cfg), Game.exe is the single-player game, and RenegadeFDS/RenegadeServer.exe is the dedicated server.

userState.evidence: literal registry paths Software\Westwood\Renegade and WOLSettings\ inside Game.exe
unresolved: no save files exist on this machine yet and the string table does not name a save folder. Will be established by measuring the first save, not assumed.

dependencies.communityReplacement: W3D Hub launcher / community GameSpy-style listings; the shipped FDS LAN mode needs no master server
dependencies.notes: Only the internet server list uses this. The in-game LAN browser discovers hosts on the local network instead.

dependencies.communityReplacement: XWIS (since EA redirected Westwood games there in 2005); not required for LAN or campaign
dependencies.notes: WOL is the only account-based path in the game. GameType = LAN in the dedicated server skips it entirely.

dependencies.service: GameSpy MOTD / version check / store links
dependencies.notes: Cosmetic. The MOTD failure path is the expected offline behaviour.

staticAnalysis.method: PE header/import parse plus ASCII string scan of all three binaries, plus INI schema read of the shipped RenegadeFDS configuration
staticAnalysis.limits: Renegade.exe is .bind-wrapped (launcher only). Game.exe and RenegadeServer.exe are readable. The LAN host implementation and its measurement are recorded in docs/preservation/03-renegade-lan.md.

notes: The dedicated server's shipped Server.ini documents GameType = WOL | GameSpy | LAN. LAN is the mode this program implements: no nickname, password, serial or login server is used.
